key_insight: WanPE turns short, ordinary text prompts into director-level cinematic plans for modern text-to-video models. It is trained at massive scale to better specify shots, camera motion, lighting, sound, and action across longer video sequences.
problem_solved: Current text-to-video systems can generate longer, more complex videos, but they still depend on prompts that are often too vague to control cinematic details consistently across multi-shot scenes. This paper addresses the need for richer prompt planning that translates a user's intent into a production-ready screenplay.
method: Introduces WanPE, a 397B-parameter prompt enhancement model for cinematic text-to-video generation.
Trains the model on 1.05M real-world videos to learn how directors structure actions, camera trajectories, lighting, and sound over time.
Enhances prompts before generation so video models receive more detailed, scene-aware instructions for multi-shot storytelling.
impact: For practitioners, WanPE could improve controllability and consistency in text-to-video workflows, especially for longer cinematic outputs. It offers a practical way to bridge the gap between user prompts and the detailed planning needed by modern generative video systems.
